extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, practitioners, deposit account holders, and USPTO filing/payments personnel
extracted.subtask_short: USPTO fees and small entity rules
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO guidance on credit-card payments, deposit account setup/use/replenishment/authorizations, penalties and refunds, and definitions/eligibility and fee reductions for small and micro entity status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Credit Card Payment Form (PTO-2038)
rubrics_metrics.description: Credit card payments for patent process or trademark process fees should be submitted in writing and preferably using the USPTO Credit Card Payment Form (PTO-2038) or via the USPTO electronic filing system; failure to use the form may result in credit card information becoming part of the public Office file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submitted PTO-2038 or other written authorization lacks the information necessary to charge the fee, the customer must submit a revised form; Office employees will not accept oral (telephonic) instructions to complete the form or otherwise charge a patent/trademark process fee. See 37 CFR 1.2 and MPEP § 607.02 for returnability of fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security code requirement for online credit card payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Credit card submissions made on the USPTO website must include the 3-digit or 4-digit security code associated with the card in addition to the card number to verify cardholder possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security code (CVV/CVV2/CVC2/CID) is required at time of Internet transaction; Discover/Mastercard/Visa use 3-digit code on the back, American Express uses 4-digit code on the front. If the security code is unreadable, contact the issuing financial institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds of credit card payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Refunds of fees paid by credit card will be made by credit to the credit card account to which the fee was charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.26 and 35 U.S.C. 42(d) apply to refunds for patent/trademark fees paid by credit card; see MPEP § 607.02 for returnability procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted credit card payments under 37 CFR 1.23
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.23 permits payment of any patent process fee, trademark process fee, or information product fee by credit card, subject to actual collection of the charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments remain subject to collection; see related rules on written authorizations and security code requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit account minimums and establishment fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposit accounts may be established upon payment of the establishing fee; a minimum deposit of $1,000 is required for paying any fee or ordering services, except a restricted subscription deposit account for patent copies may be established with $300.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A $10 charge (37 CFR 1.21(b)(1)) is assessed for opening each new account. At the end of each month a deposit account statement will be rendered and remittance must be made promptly to restore normal deposit value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly statements, prompt replenishment, and required balance
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposit account holder will receive a monthly statement and must promptly remit to restore the account to its normal deposit value; an amount sufficient to cover all requested fees/services must always be on deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charges to accounts with insufficient funds will not be accepted; failure to timely replenish can cause surcharges, suspension, or abandonment consequences for filings/payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods and required information for deposit account replenishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposit accounts may be replenished by (1) Fedwire electronic funds transfer (must supply bank name 'Treas NYC', routing code 021030004, USPTO account number 13100001, and the deposit account holder's company name and deposit account number), (2) electronic funds transfer over the USPTO website, or (3) mail to Mail Stop Deposit Accounts at the USPTO address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For delivery-service (FedEx/UPS/DHL/etc.) shipments, send to the Customer Service Window with 'Mail Stop Deposit Accounts' included. Failure to include the proper deposit account number delays processing. Contact the Deposit Account Division for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of overdrawn accounts and processing refusals
rubrics_metrics.description: An overdrawn account will be immediately suspended and no charges accepted until a proper balance is restored together with payment of $10 (37 CFR 1.21(b)(1)) to cover Office work; if a replenishment payment is refused (insufficient funds/stop payment), the processing-refusal fee under 37 CFR 1.21(m) will be charged to the deposit account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated suspensions may lead to account closure. If an authorization to charge a basic filing fee is attempted against insufficient funds, a surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) is required in addition to the required fee(s). Failure to timely pay filing fees and surcharges may result in abandonment of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized users and name matching for deposit accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized users for a deposit account must be listed in Financial Manager as authorized fee payers; Office personnel will accept obvious variations in given names provided the last/family name matches an authorized fee payer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the last name in a signed fee authorization document does not match any authorized fee payer for the deposit account, payment may be delayed or rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and limits of general authorizations to charge deposit accounts (37 CFR 1.25(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A general authorization to charge all fees, or only certain fees, set forth in 37 CFR §§ 1.16–1.18 to a deposit account may be filed in an individual application for the entire pendency or for a particular paper; such authorizations will be interpreted to cover fees set forth in 37 CFR 1.16 and 1.17 but will not apply to document supply fees (1.19), certain post-issuance fees (1.20), or most miscellaneous fees (1.21) except the processing fee under 1.21(m) for refused/charged-back checks or credit cards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An authorization to charge the basic filing fee will be treated as authorization to charge the basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, any excess claims fees, application size fee, and any non-electronic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16). An authorization to charge issue fees (37 CFR 1.18) may be filed only after mailing of the notice of allowance; a general authorization made prior to mailing of the notice does not apply to issue fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of authorizations for national stage and international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An authorization to charge fees under 37 CFR 1.16 in an application entering the U.S. national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371 will be treated as an authorization to charge fees under 37 CFR 1.492; authorizations to charge fees in an international design application under 37 CFR 1.1031 will be effective only for the transmittal fee (1.1031(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This treatment recognizes the necessity of timely national-stage fee payment to avoid abandonment and addresses differences in which fees apply in national-stage and international filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and specificity requirement for deposit account authorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposit account authorizations must be clear and unambiguous; ambiguous authorizations that deviate from usual forms may not be interpreted as applicants intend and may result in returned fees and additional expenses or petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample authorization wording is given in the guidance (e.g., authorizing the Director to charge any fees under specified CFR paragraphs). If an authorization purports to charge 'the filing fee' the Office will treat that as covering specified fees under 37 CFR 1.16 unless the authorization expressly limits coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surcharge for attempted charge against insufficient deposit account funds
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is an authorization to charge a basic filing fee to a deposit account which is overdrawn or has insufficient funds, a surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) is required in addition to payment of the basic filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on or after July 1, 2005 that have been accorded a filing date, if an authorization to charge the basic filing, search, or examination fee is attempted against insufficient funds, the surcharge under 1.16(f) applies. Payment of surcharge and fees must be timely to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds to deposit accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Refunds to a deposit account are handled as set forth in MPEP § 607.02 and corresponding CFR provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult MPEP § 607.02 for procedures and conditions for returnability and refund to deposit accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity fee reductions: scope, amounts, and effective changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 41(h) and implementing regulations, many patent fees are reduced for qualifying small entities (persons, small business concerns, nonprofit organizations); as of December 29, 2022 most applicable fees were reduced by 60 percent (increased from 50%), and an 80 percent reduction applies to the filing fee for an electronically-filed nonprovisional original utility application by a small entity (per amendment to 35 U.S.C. 41(h)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees reduced by 60% include application filing fees (basic filing, search, examination, application size, excess claims), certain extension and petition fees, issue fees, maintenance fees, appeals fees, and others listed (see 37 CFR 1.16, 1.17, 1.18, 1.20, 41.20). Some fees remain ineligible for reduction (document supply fees under 1.19, certificate of correction fees 1.20(a), most miscellaneous fees 1.21), though some sequence-listing and other specific fees may be reduced. Effective dates for particular fee changes (e.g., PCT-related reductions) are specified in CFR references.

rubrics_metrics.name: General definition of small entity (37 CFR 1.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: For fee reduction purposes a 'small entity' under 37 CFR 1.27(a) means any party that qualifies as a person, a small business concern, or a nonprofit organization as set out in paragraphs (a)(1)–(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'person' is used broadly to cover individuals who may have acquired rights in the invention even if not inventors themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'person' for small entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'person' means any inventor or other individual who has not assigned, granted, conveyed, or licensed, and is under no obligation to assign/grant/convey/license, rights in the invention; an individual who has transferred some rights may still qualify if all transferees also qualify as small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation contemplates that transferred rights do not necessarily preclude small entity status if all holders of rights remain qualifying small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'small business concern' for small entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'small business concern' must not have assigned or be obligated to assign rights to any entity that would not qualify as a small entity and must meet the size standards set forth in 13 CFR 121.801–121.805 to be eligible for reduced patent fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions about size standards should be directed to the SBA Office of Size Standards; meeting federal size standards is a prerequisite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'nonprofit organization' for small entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprofit organization includes (i) universities or other institutions of higher education meeting specific criteria (regular student admissions with secondary education certificate, authorization to provide post-secondary education, degree or 2-year program awarding, nonprofit status, accreditation or preaccreditation), (ii) organizations described in 26 U.S.C. 501(c)(3) and exempt under 501(a), and (iii) certain nonprofit scientific or educational organizations, including foreign equivalents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations strictly research/manufacturing/service facilities are not intended to be included unless they meet the educational/institutional definitions. Foreign nonprofits that would qualify if located in the U.S. may also qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Government use license exceptions to small entity disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain government use licenses do not preclude claiming small entity status: e.g., use license resulting from rights determination under Executive Order 10096 in accordance with §501.60, use license resulting from 15 U.S.C. 3710d(a) when the Federal employee-inventor retains title as authorized, or use licenses arising under specified actions in funding agreements (35 U.S.C. 202 provisions) subject to enumerated conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed subconditions apply (e.g., inventions made solely by employees of the small entity, Federal agency actions assigning rights back to the small entity, CRADA-related waivers). Even if an exception applies, no refund under § 1.28(a) is available for any patent fee paid by the Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights in the invention and effect of transfers/licenses/security interests
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'rights in the invention' refer to rights in the United States (exclude rights transferred abroad) and ownership or assignment/licensing of such rights to a non-small entity will disqualify an applicant from claiming small entity status; a security interest does not constitute an obligation to transfer unless defaulted upon, and default may cause loss of small entity status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rights are transferred to a non-small entity and later returned so all rights are again held by small entities, reduced fees may be reclaimed. A non-exclusive license to a non-small entity will disqualify small entity status (e.g., Ulead Systems v. Lex Computer & Management cited). Notification of loss of entitlement due to default on security interest must be filed under 37 CFR 1.27(g) prior to paying the earliest affected fee (issue or maintenance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro entity status reference and relation to small entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who qualify as a small entity may also qualify for micro entity status under 35 U.S.C. 123, which provides additional fee reductions; requirements for micro entity status are in 37 CFR 1.29 and MPEP § 509.04 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the cited CFR and MPEP sections for eligibility criteria and documentation required to claim micro entity status.
